overview.description: This guide provides instructions for testing Ansible playbooks in different environments before deploying them to IBM Technology Zone. Testing ensures playbooks work correctly and helps identify issues early in the development process.

testing_scenarios.scenario: Testing playbooks inside VMs (Base VM platforms)
Testing playbooks locally on Mac for Account Vending

vm_testing.title: Testing Ansible Playbooks Inside VMs
vm_testing.description: For Base VM platforms (OCPV VM, VPC VM), you can test playbooks directly inside the provisioned VM before finalizing your environment definition.

prerequisites.prerequisite: Provisioned VM from IBM Technology Zone

actions.action: SSH into your VM using the provided credentials
Or use the web-based terminal if available in IBM Technology Zone

step.title: Elevate Privileges
step.description: Gain root access for playbook execution
step.note: Ansible playbooks for VMs typically require root privileges to install packages and configure system settings.

step.title: Navigate to Post-Deploy Directory
step.description: Change to the post-deploy directory where playbooks are executed
step.note: The post-deploy directory is where IBM Technology Zone executes playbooks during environment provisioning.

step.title: Upload Latest Playbook
step.description: Transfer your updated playbook.yaml file to the VM

method.name: scp
method.description: Secure copy from your local machine

method.name: vi_editor
method.note: Paste your playbook content and save

method.name: curl
method.description: Download from a URL (e.g., GitHub raw file)

step.title: Create Test Variables File
step.note: Use the same variable names that your playbook expects. These simulate the variables that would be passed from the environment definition.

step.title: Execute Playbook
step.description: Run the playbook with your test variables

alternative_inline_vars.note: Use this format for quick tests with few variables

what_to_check.check: All tasks completed successfully (no failed tasks)

step.title: Iterate and Fix Issues
step.description: If errors occur, update the playbook and test again

issue.solution: Verify package name and repository availability
Check service logs and configuration files

best_practices.practice: Test with realistic variable values that match production
Test all conditional branches in your playbook
Verify idempotency by running the playbook multiple times
Check system logs for any warnings or errors
Test the post-deploy output file displays correctly

issue.name: playbook_not_found
issue.symptom: Error: Could not find or access 'playbook.yaml'
issue.solution: Verify you're in the correct directory and file was uploaded successfully

issue.name: json_parse_error
issue.solution: Validate JSON syntax using jq or online validator

local_mac_testing.title: Testing Ansible Playbooks Locally on Mac for Account Vending
local_mac_testing.description: For Account Vending and IBM Cloud Services platforms, you can test playbooks locally on your Mac by pointing to an existing IBM Cloud account. This allows rapid iteration without waiting for full environment provisioning.

prerequisites.prerequisite: IBM Cloud account with appropriate services

step.title: Provision Account Vending Environment
step.description: Create a test environment in IBM Technology Zone with the services you need

actions.action: Set post_deploy_display_variables to true in environment definition

critical_setting.name: post_deploy_display_variables
critical_setting.purpose: This setting causes IBM Technology Zone to display all deployment variables on the reservation output page, which you'll need for local testing.

step.title: Install Ansible on Mac
step.description: Install Ansible using Homebrew package manager

step.title: Copy Variables from Reservation Output
step.description: Navigate to your IBM Technology Zone reservation and copy the displayed variables

actions.action: Go to your reservation in IBM Technology Zone
Copy all the JSON variables displayed
Save to a file or prepare to share with Bob

step.note: These variables contain the actual IBM Cloud account information and service details from your provisioned environment.

step.title: Format Variables for Testing
step.description: Ask Bob to format the copied variables into a structure suitable for local testing
step.user_prompt_example:
"Bob, I copied these variables from my IBM Technology Zone reservation. Please format them for local Ansible playbook testing:
[paste your copied variables here]"

bob_will_create.file: Properly formatted JSON file with all necessary variables
Optional wrapper playbook that sets up the variable structure

formatting_requirements.requirement: Convert string-encoded JSON to proper JSON objects
Ensure all six variable types are included

step.title: Create Test Directory
step.description: Set up a local directory for testing

step.title: Test the Playbook
step.description: Execute the playbook locally using the formatted variables

command_options.option: -vv - Verbose output for debugging (use -vvv for more detail)
--check - Dry run mode (doesn't make actual changes)
--diff - Show differences in files being changed

dry_run_first.purpose: Test what would happen without making actual changes to your IBM Cloud account

step.title: Review Results
step.description: Check the playbook execution and verify changes

check_ibm_cloud.description: Verify changes in IBM Cloud console

step.title: Iterate and Refine
step.description: Make improvements based on test results

best_practices.practice: Always use --check mode first to preview changes
Test with a dedicated test IBM Cloud account if possible
Keep test variables file secure (contains API keys)
Use verbose mode (-vv or -vvv) for debugging
Test error handling by simulating failures
Verify idempotency by running playbook multiple times

consideration.name: Protect API Keys
consideration.description: The test_variables.json file contains IBM Cloud API keys and sensitive data

actions.action: Never commit test_variables.json to version control
Use restrictive file permissions: chmod 600 test_variables.json

consideration.name: Test Account Isolation
consideration.description: Use a separate test account to avoid affecting production resources

consideration.name: Cost Management
consideration.description: Be aware that testing may create billable resources in IBM Cloud

actions.action: Use free tier services when possible
Clean up test resources after testing

solutions.solution: Verify API key is correct and not expired
Check that API key has necessary permissions
Ensure account_apikey variable is properly set

issue.name: variable_parsing_error
issue.symptom: Error parsing variables or undefined variables

solutions.solution: Validate JSON syntax with: cat test_variables.json | jq .
Ensure all required variable types are present
Check for proper string escaping in JSON
For IBM Cloud: ansible-galaxy collection install ibm.cloudcollection
For URI module: Included in ansible-core

issue.name: connection_timeout
issue.symptom: Timeout connecting to IBM Cloud APIs

vm_testing.use_when: Testing software installation and system configuration
Verifying playbook works in actual VM environment

advantages.advantage: No need to provision full environment each time
Can use version control for test files
